svg.title: Code review as gatekeeping vs teaching
svg.desc: Two sets of review comments on the same pull request. The gatekeeping review says "This is wrong", "Rewrote it, use my version" and "Why would you do it like this?", with no reasons and no difference between blocking and optional points. The teaching review labels each comment: a must-fix that explains why (no timeout on an upstream call means one slow system stalls the response) and links the standard, an optional nit, a question that builds judgement (what happens if the upstream times out?), and praise for a good test. A note says to pair instead of writing 40 comments and to turn repeated comments into a checklist or lint rule.
svg.text: Review comments that grow people
Same pull request. One review gatekeeps, the other teaches.
❌ Gatekeeping
"This is wrong."
No reason, no link. They learn nothing.
"Rewrote it, use my version."
Rescue, not growth.
"Why would you do it like this?"
Sounds like blame, not a question.
Every comment looks blocking, so the author
can't tell what really matters.
✅ Teaching
Must-fix
No timeout on this upstream call, so one
slow system stalls the whole response. See the
resilience standard (link).
Nit
Optional: a clearer name would help here.
Question
What happens if the upstream times out?
Nice
The retry test covers the DLQ path. Good call.
Big gap? Pair instead of writing 40 comments.
Repeated comment? Turn it into a checklist item or a lint rule.
